title: Controlplane heartbeat loss investigation - notes and runbook draft
body:
Summary:

On 2026-03-10 ~08:15 UTC we observed repeated short (30s-90s) control-plane heartbeat failures from a subset of private deployments in eu-west-1. Symptoms: control plane metric 'heartbeat_missed' spiked, private agent reported 'controlplane unreachable' and routing fallback to public proxy occurred for ~17% of requests for affected customers. No host-level CPU/GPU saturation observed. Impact window: 08:12-09:05 UTC with multiple flapping periods.

Why this doc exists:
- Capture timeline and triage notes from on-call shifts (Riley -> Aisha -> Diego)
- Draft a short runbook checklist for future hits
- Propose mitigations (quick-fix and long-term) and owners

Top-level hypothesis (final RCA pending):
- A combination of a customer-side network policy change (tightened firewall egress rules for ephemeral ports) plus a VPC route propagation quirk after a controller node reboot caused asymmetric pathing and TCP handshake failures for our control-plane heartbeat protocol (aggressive short-lived TCP connections).
- Evidence: tcpdump from affected agents shows SYNs leaving but no SYN-ACK, or SYN-ACK coming from a different IP/interface and being dropped by conntrack/iptables on the agent side; traceroutes show different egress IPs pre/post-event.

Timeline (detailed):
- 2026-03-10 08:11:52 UTC: first alert from metrics pipeline (heartbeat_missed > 5/min) for 3 customers in eu-west-1
- 08:12:10: oncall (Riley) starts investigation; checks console (overview dashboard) -> sees per-route spike in latency and fallback events
- 08:14:00: request logs show sudden increase in 'controlplane_fallback' for customers with private deployments behind corporate firewalls
- 08:16:30: ssh to one affected agent host (private tenant A) - no obvious resource pressure; connected to customer VPN to validate visibility
- 08:20:10: tcpdump capturing on agent: SYN seen to controlplane-ip:443, no SYN-ACK; same capture shows some SYN-ACKs but with unexpected source IP (NAT) then RST later
- 08:26:00: cross-check with customer network team: customer reports they rolled out an egress firewall change at ~08:10 that restricted ephemeral port ranges for outbound connections
- 08:31:00: reproduce: from agent host, traceroute to controlplane shows different path; MTU tests (ping -M do -s) show no fragmentation but some ICMP unreachable intermittently
- 08:45:00: applied temporary mitigation: route traffic via public proxy (policy set to 'failover: public') for affected tenants to restore connectivity; observed fallbacks cleared impact
- 09:02:00: controlplane team restarted an edge controller node as part of unrelated maintenance; route tables re-propagated at 09:04 causing transient asymmetric routes but did not reintroduce the failure after firewall rollback

Key evidence files (collected):
- tcpdump-agentA-2026-03-10.pcap (shows SYN w/ no SYN-ACK)
- traceroute-agentA-prepost.txt (diff of routing)
- cloudroute-delta-logs-09-04.txt

Root cause analysis (current):
1) Customer firewall change restricted outbound ephemeral ports and/or performed asymmetric NAT. Our heartbeat protocol uses short-lived outbound connections to controlplane on 443, relying on NAT symmetry and ephemeral port mapping to be stable across retries. When the mapping changed or return traffic appeared to come from a different NAT endpoint, conntrack on the agent dropped packets invoking a reset.
2) A coincident route propagation event (edge controller reboot) changed the upstream egress path which increased likelihood that response packets would arrive via an interface with different conntrack expectations.

Why this caused heartbeat misses but not full failure:
- Heartbeat protocol has retries; intermittent failures caused missed heartbeats but fallbacks kept request traffic alive by switching route. Because the issue was at the network/NAT layer, application logs remained mostly green.

Short-term mitigations applied during incident:
- Failover to public proxy for affected customers (policy change) -> immediate reduction in missing heartbeats
- Temporarily increased heartbeat timeout and retry window for affected tenants (config override) to reduce noise while customer firewall change was validated
- Coordinated with customer network team; customer began rolling back the restrictive rule at 08:38 and full rollback confirmed at 08:55

Runbook draft (quick checklist to add to SRE oncall playbook):
1) Alert triage: check 'heartbeat_missed' dashboard, scope by region + tenant
2) If > X tenants show simultaneous misses in same region:
   - SSH to one affected agent host and run: sudo tcpdump -i any 'tcp and (host CONTROLPLANE_IP)' -w /tmp/cp.pcap
   - Run traceroute + mtr to controlplane ip: traceroute -n CONTROLPLANE_IP; mtr -c 20 CONTROLPLANE_IP
   - Check iptables/conntrack counters: sudo conntrack -C; sudo conntrack -L | head -n 40; sudo iptables -L -v -n
3) Quick hypothesis checks: do we see SYNs without SYN-ACKs? are SYN-ACKs coming from a different source IP?
4) If asymmetric NAT/ephemeral-port suspicion: ask customer network team if any egress NAT or firewall rules changed and if they restrict ephemeral ports or permit return IP ranges.
5) Failover step: set route policy to 'force public' for tenant (config path: /ops/tenants/<tenant>/network/policy) and monitor heartbeat metrics for improvement
6) Temporary config workarounds: increase heartbeat timeout (config key: controlplane.heartbeat.timeout) and raise retry backoff to 2x for 30 minutes
7) If host-level conntrack counters high: run 'sudo conntrack -F' only after coordination and during low traffic window; document risk
8) After resolution: collect pcaps, traceroutes, route diffs; create postmortem ticket and notify customer success with a short blurb

Quick commands cheat-sheet (to paste into pager):
- tcpdump: sudo tcpdump -i any -s 0 -w /tmp/cp.pcap 'tcp and (host CONTROLPLANE_IP)'
- traceroute: traceroute -n CONTROLPLANE_IP
- mtr: mtr -c 20 -r CONTROLPLANE_IP
- conntrack count: sudo conntrack -C
- conntrack list (filter by dst): sudo conntrack -L | grep CONTROLPLANE_IP -A 30
- iptables: sudo iptables -S; sudo iptables -L -v -n

Post-incident action items (owners + due):
- Aisha: finalize RCA doc and link PCAPs; add final root cause paragraph to SRE postmortem (due 2026-03-14)
- Diego: update the oncall runbook with the checklist above and add playbook snippets to the pager (due 2026-03-18)
- Marta: implement a telemetry alert for 'asymmetric-responses' signature (SYNs without SYN-ACKs for X secs) and add dashboard tile (due 2026-04-01)
- Samir (net infra): investigate whether edge controller restarts can be sequenced to avoid route churn during tenant-sensitive windows; propose change (due 2026-03-25)
- Product: review heartbeat protocol for adding optional persistent TCP connections or keep-alive to reduce short-lived conntrack sensitivity (assigned to PM: Lena H. - due 2026-05-01)

Lessons learned / notes to keep in mind:
- Short-lived outbound connection patterns are more brittle for private deployments behind customer NATs / strict egress policies. Consider offering a 'keep-alive-proxy' mode for private tenants where we maintain a persistent, pinned connection through the permitted egress path.
- Observability: we need a lightweight network-path signature in metrics (SYN-without-SYNACK counter) surfaced in console so customers and SRE can quickly identify NAT asymmetry events.
- Coordination: Always check customer change windows first; customers sometimes apply egress changes without traffic-management coordination. Improve CS playbook to require notification before changing egress/NAT rules that affect control-plane IP ranges.

Open questions / unresolved:
- Exact conntrack/iptables rule that dropped mirrored responses: need kernel-level trace from agent host during the event (requires enabling netfilter logging on a repro box)
- Whether we should change default ephemeral port ranges on our agents or recommend that customers allow wide ephemeral ranges
- Whether we should move heartbeat to a UDP-based lighter-weight protocol (trade-offs exist)

Appendix (raw notes):
- Agent tcpdump excerpt: 
  08:19:12.123456 IP 10.10.23.45.54832 > 3.7.12.97.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 123456 ecr 0,nop,wscale 7], length 0
  (no SYN-ACK observed in subsequent 5s)
- Trace pre-event: 10.10.23.45 -> 192.0.2.1 -> 198.51.100.7 (controlplane)
- Trace mid-event: 10.10.23.45 -> 198.51.100.9 -> 198.51.100.7 (different NAT egress)

If you're the oncall reading this: steps in order of ops priority:
1) scope (dashboard) -> 2) collect pcaps/traces -> 3) failover to public proxy -> 4) reach out to customer network -> 5) increase heartbeat windows -> 6) collect artifacts -> 7) back to normal and start RCA ticket

Notes-to-self: be concise in the customer-facing postmortem. They care about whether we changed anything on our side (we did only fallback routing + heartbeat timeout) and how we will prevent recurrence (runbook + telemetry + product changes).

End of notes.
_comment: Document created as an iterative incident review and runbook draft for private/VPC control plane reachability issues. Keep this in Drive as a working doc until RCA finalized.
